newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn working behind scenes for Mideast peace - Kohl.
newsitem.headline: Bonn working behind scenes for Mideast peace - Kohl.

text.p: Germany has been working hard behind the scenes to help peace talks in the Middle East, Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Thursday.

Kohl told a New Year news conference that Germany and the European Union had a contribution to make to peace in the region, but that he saw no need for them to make a large public show of their activity.
"In the last few weeks Germany has done a whole lot in this area," he said, declining to give details except to say that more was likely to become public in the next few weeks.

Late last year Germany played host to Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in short succession to try to press both sides to revive the stalled peace process.

It has also provided the largest share of EU aid to the region and sponsored talks on the problematic issue of water rights. But it has left the business of Western political meditation to the United States.

Kohl's approach is in marked contrast to that of French President Jacques Chirac, who made a tumultuous tour to the Middle East last October with the stated aim of increasing Europe's political role in Arab-Israeli peace negotiations.

Chirac received enthusiastic mass welcomes in Damascus, the West Bank and Gaza and clashed with heavy-handed Israeli security men hindering his contact with Palestinians, leaving Israelis with little confidence in his impartiality.
